holds.issue: The John 2 Temple cleansing has been moved into PUBLIC in its Johannine narrative position after Cana. Whether it is a distinct historical cleansing or the same episode as the Synoptic Passion accounts remains an unresolved exegetical question.
holds.requiredAction: Keep the PUBLIC placement explicitly qualified as Johannine narrative order, not proof of precise historical dating or one-versus-two cleansings. Review the source relationship before theatre publication.

presentationDecision.displayRule: Display John 2:13–22 after Cana only as John's narrative order, without asserting whether a separate historical cleansing occurred.
presentationDecision.withheldClaim: One-cleansing or two-cleansing harmonisation, precise historical date, and Passion-era relocation.

holds.issue: The John 20 cinematic scene now describes the empty tomb and appearance to Mary Magdalene. Artwork must not imply John 20 narrates an eyewitness account of the instant of Resurrection.
holds.requiredAction: Review depiction and licensing of any cinematic artwork against John 20:1–18 and keep the source-note visible.

presentationDecision.displayRule: Illustrate the empty tomb and risen Christ appearing to Mary Magdalene; do not depict an eyewitness view of the instant of Resurrection as John 20:1–18.
presentationDecision.withheldClaim: Scripture-backed depiction of the exact moment of Resurrection, and unlicensed art publication.

holds.issue: A single scene has an exact citation plus a secondary overlapping hidden-life citation; not one automatic canonical identity.
holds.requiredAction: Adjudicate exact Temple episode and overlapping hidden-life transition independently.

presentationDecision.displayRule: Use Luke 2:41–52 for the finding in the Temple and Luke 2:51–52 for the overlapping return to Nazareth. Retain separate IDs and suppress an automatic multi-candidate scene jump.
presentationDecision.withheldClaim: Treating Luke 2:51–52 as an independent second Temple finding or one unambiguous scene identity.

holds.issue: The Magi and Presentation chronology compares different Evangelists; narrative order is not an explicitly supplied single-Gospel dating.
holds.requiredAction: Specify conservative harmony basis or avoid asserted precise order/dates.

presentationDecision.displayRule: Keep the Magi (Matthew 2) and the Presentation (Luke 2) as distinct Evangelist narratives; state that visual succession is reading order, not an established dated harmony.
presentationDecision.withheldClaim: A date-certain itinerary or Gospel-proven relative timing for Magi versus Presentation.

holds.issue: The Johannine cleansing is now in PUBLIC, but selected public-ministry chapters retain differences between the canonical chronology and the 181-scene study order across Gospel narratives.
holds.requiredAction: Review chronology and source-specific narrative order without imposing unsupported cross-Gospel dates or identifying distinct Gospel accounts by citation similarity.

presentationDecision.displayRule: Preserve cited within-Gospel narrative precedence and the stable 151 event keys, without imposing one dated global Matthew–Mark–Luke–John chronology.
presentationDecision.withheldClaim: Full historical cross-Gospel harmonisation, source-free chronology, or conflating event identities by passage overlap.
